source.title_on_document: Interactions with generative AI chatbots: unveiling dialogic dynamics, students' perceptions, and practical competencies in creative problem-solving

supplement.where: No online supplement is mentioned. The appendix (Tables 8, 9, 10: questionnaire, interview outline, proposal marking criteria) is inside this PDF, pp. 25-26. Data 'available upon reasonable request' (p. 27).
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the PDF. The appendix holds instruments only, no extra statistics.

paper_design_summary: Eighty first-semester PhD students at a Chinese university were assigned (the paper says randomly, while calling the design quasi-experimental) to either five weekly half-hour dialogue sessions with the Dou Bao GAI chatbot (n = 40) or five sessions with a self-chosen peer (n = 40), over three months, to develop an innovative research proposal. Two independent markers scored each student's final proposal on a 100-point rubric (objectives, questions and hypotheses, literature review, design and methods, originality), compared by ANCOVA controlling for a pretest score on the proposal each student wrote for the PhD application. The paper also codes dialogue transcripts and surveys perceptions (self-report).

studies.label: GAI chatbot (Dou Bao) vs peer dialogue for a PhD research proposal

assignment.what_was_assigned: Individual students to the experimental group (dialogue with the Dou Bao GAI chatbot) or the control group (dialogue with one self-chosen peer)
assignment.quote: Then they were randomly assigned to either the experimental or the control group, each comprising 40 students.
assignment.locator: p. 8, Methodology, Participants. The paper also states 'This study adopted a quasi-experimental approach' (p. 8, Procedure) and 'We used quasi-experiments' (p. 1, Abstract)

arms.name: Experimental group (student-GAI chatbot)
arms.description: Five weekly half-hour individual dialogue sessions with the Dou Bao chatbot (ByteDance), by text or speech, on five themes (research topic, research questions, literature, research design, originality), aimed at an innovative and practical research proposal; after a 3-hour training session given to all participants

arms.name: Control group (student-peer)
arms.description: Same schedule and themes, but each student chose one peer for dialogue; no access to GAI chatbots or similar tools during the study period

participants.exclusions: None reported for the proposal outcome (Table 7, N = 40 per group). The perception survey (Table 6) reports N = 36 per group without explaining the 4 missing per group.
participants.who: First-semester PhD students (32 male, 48 female, aged 26-31) in international education, student development, educational leadership and management, and curriculum development and pedagogy; volunteers; none had used GAI chatbots for CPS tasks before
participants.country: China (a Project 211 university in southern China)
participants.quote: In total, 80 postgraduate students pursuing PhD degrees participated in this study.

ai_tool.name_model: Dou Bao (ByteDance GAI chatbot built on large language models)
ai_tool.how_used: Individual dialogue with the chatbot, by typed text or speech, in five arranged weekly half-hour sessions on set proposal themes; transcripts audio-recorded and coded (p. 9, Procedure step 3)

task.description: Create an innovative and practical research proposal (creative problem-solving task); pretest = proposal written for the PhD application, post-test = new proposal submitted at the end based on the discussions with Dou Bao or a peer
task.duration: 3-hour training, then five weekly half-hour interactions; whole experiment three months (September to December)

outcomes.name: Research proposal total score (practical performance in CPS)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two independent markers scored anonymised proposals with the Table 10 rubric: five dimensions (research objectives; research questions and hypotheses; literature review; research design and methods; originality of research), each 20 points at four levels (20/15/10/5), total 100; Kappa 0.83. Only one of five dimensions is originality; the rest are quality. Dimension scores are not reported separately. The paper says the 'overall grade (total score) was calculated as the average score of each marking criteria score' while also describing a 100-point total. Markers' expertise is not described; coded expert_raters because they marked with criteria and model proposals, which is a guess (pp. 12, 26).
outcomes.delay: Submitted at the end of the three-month experiment, after the five sessions; the paper does not say whether the chatbot was still available while the final proposal was written

contrasts.reported: Table 7 ANCOVA (covariate: pretest score): Experimental group N = 40, Mean 57.77, SD 11.79; Control group N = 40, Mean 46.38, SD 12.85; df 1; F = 15.058 (p < 0.001); Partial eta^2 0.179 (text: 'Partial eta^2 = 0.17'). Levene F = 0.337, p = 0.568; homogeneity of slopes F = 1.734, p = 0.192. Whether the means are raw or covariate-adjusted is not stated; pretest means are not reported.

company_involvement.description: No company involvement stated. The tool is ByteDance's Dou Bao; funding is the National Natural Science Foundation of China (62377014); authors declare no conflict of interest.
company_involvement.locator: p. 9; p. 27, Funding and Competing interests

eligibility.reason: The paper states that the 80 students were randomly assigned, 40 per group, to a GAI chatbot or a peer partner (p. 8), although it labels the design quasi-experimental; 80 people are analyzed (Table 7, p. 20); the outcome is a marker-scored research proposal (a research-idea task) whose rubric includes originality (Table 10, p. 26). Caveats: the creativity content of the score is one fifth of a mostly quality rubric, the control condition is a human partner (ai_vs_active), and no randomization procedure or balance table is given.

one_line_finding: PhD students who developed a research proposal over five sessions with the Dou Bao chatbot scored 57.77 (SD 11.79, n = 40) versus 46.38 (SD 12.85, n = 40) for those working with a peer, ANCOVA F = 15.058, p < 0.001, partial eta^2 = 0.179 (p. 20, Table 7).
open_questions: Is a 100-point proposal-quality rubric in which originality is one of five 20-point dimensions a creativity outcome (overall_creativity) or a quality outcome (usefulness/other)?

Design class: the paper says 'randomly assigned' but calls the study quasi-experimental and gives no randomization procedure. field_rct vs lab_rct vs quasi_people needs a decision; I chose field_rct because the task (a PhD research proposal) ran over a semester in the students' doctoral program.
Were the Table 7 means raw or ANCOVA-adjusted? The paper does not say.
Control students chose their own peer; the paper does not say whether peers were other control participants, which would make control outcomes non-independent.

Was the chatbot available while the final proposal was written? Fig. 1 calls it a 'post-test'; step 5 says the proposal was 'based on the discussions undertaken with either Dou Bao or a peer'. If not available, the outcome would be after_ai.
notes: Other outcomes not listed because they are not scored on the creative output: dialogue-dynamics coding of transcripts (Tables 2-5, Figs. 2-3; percentages of coding categories such as speculation, which are process measures), and perceived usefulness, ease of use, and intention to use (Table 6, self-report, N = 36 per group). Eighteen experimental students were interviewed. The candidate record says Holzner et al. 2025 coded this paper as CP08.
